name: How Long Should a Kitchen Remodeling Estimate Take to Prepare?

mainEntity.name: How long should a contractor take to prepare a detailed written kitchen remodeling estimate after an on-site visit?
mainEntity.text: How long should a contractor take to prepare a detailed written kitchen remodeling estimate after an on-site visit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Estimate timing varies with the amount of information required. A simple cabinet or countertop update may be priced quickly, while a kitchen involving layout changes, electrical work, plumbing, structural questions, custom cabinetry, or multiple selections requires more coordination. The contractor should explain what the estimate includes and what remains provisional. Before the site visit, prepare measurements if available, appliance specifications, inspiration images, preferred materials, budget range, and must-have features. Ask the contractor to confirm the scope, measurement method, allowance assumptions, expected proposal date, and price-validity period. Material costs and supplier availability can change, so determine whether the estimate is fixed for a stated period or subject to revision. Do not select a contractor solely because a proposal arrives fastest. A one-page total delivered immediately may omit items that a careful estimate identifies. Conversely, an extended delay without updates can signal weak project management. Request written notice when the scope or assumptions change, and compare estimates only after each contractor has received the same project information. A reasonable preparation period should result in a clear, reviewable document.
acceptedAnswer.description: The time depends on project complexity, measurements, design selections, trade coordination, and permitting assumptions. A detailed estimate may require more time than a rough budget. Ask when the proposal will arrive, how long its pricing remains valid, and what information is still missing.
